response.answer: Data governance under PIPL requires consent for minors, incident response, retention limits, and cross-agency sharing agreements. Explicit consent is needed for sensitive data and international transfers. Compliance with PIPL includes maintaining processing records.

results.title: Navigating China's Personal Information Protection Law
results.content: # Ultimate Guide to PIPL Compliance: Navigating China's Personal Information Protection Law. The global surge in cross-border data flow has prompted governments worldwide, including China, to intensify oversight of data export and enhance security provisions. Under China's Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL), obtaining consent for data handling is pivotal. * Regulations to Promote and Standardize Cross-Border Data Flows; * Undergo Personal Information Protection Certification; or, * Form a contract with the foreign recipient ensuring compliance with PIPL standards. * Remote access to important data and PI stored in China by a person or entity located outside of China - this is to say, if an overseas party within the same or different company, remotely accesses the Important Data or PI of an individual located in China, then this activity will also constitute cross-border data transfer, even if the data is not actively exported to a location outside of China. PIPL mandates that organizations conduct a Personal Information Protection Impact Assessment (PIPIA) in various scenarios, including handling sensitive information, using PI for automated decision-making, disclosing PI to third parties, and transferring PI internationally. China's Personal Information Protection Law (PIPL) has significantly reshaped the data security legislation.

results.title: Data protection laws in China
results.content: In certain circumstances, such as collecting or processing sensitive personal information, overseas data transfers and direct marketing, separate consent (i.e. explicit consent specific to the processing activity / transfer (rather than just general consent to the privacy notice, expressed through an affirmative action) is required from the data subject. In addition to obtaining consent, a data controller (i.e. the organization who has the authority to determine the purposes, means or method of processing) should provide data subjects with a privacy policy or other form of notice, informing them of the scope and ways in which their personal information is collected, processed and disclosed, including the following information:. * perform a personal information impact assessment (PIIA), and take effective measures to protect the data subjects according to the assessment results (e.g. putting in place a data transfer agreement or similar contractual protections) (see Collection & Processing);.
